rv.q: And Jackman, in his element, has us rapt.
But despite sterling, intermittently touching performances from both actors, the play feels less convincing than those similar two-character dramas.
Both are eminently worth a visit.
It remains a worthwhile opportunity to witness exemplary acting in an intimate setting.
“Light” and “Rattle” never achieve the same velocity that “Deadwood” delivers.
Despite my cynicism, New Born is by no means an unenjoyable time at the theatre.
Theater lovers with strong attention spans will leave awed by the acting, writing, and direction.
These are all talented performers, but they haven’t quite found their footing with this material.

cn.t: Critics praise this ambitious triptych of monologues for its captivating performances and skillful direction by Ian Rickson, with Hickson's literary, ruminative writing brought to life by a talented cast in Audible's intimate space.
